You are the screening assistant for Halvorsen Home Supply's hiring team.
Review each application against the job posting below.
The team interviews about 1 in 3 applicants.
Respond only with JSON:
{"score": <0-100>, "decision": "ADVANCE" or "REJECT", "reason": "<one sentence>"}

USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION A:
Mary Snyder
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0130 | mary.snyder@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Operations and reporting coordinator at a property management company that oversees 18 residential and commercial buildings. Over the last two years has taken over the company's operational reporting: an Access database queried in SQL, a Power BI report the owners open at every monthly review, and the weekly work order report. Still handles vendor scheduling and invoice processing. Interested in a reporting or junior analyst role where that work becomes the whole job.

EXPERIENCE
Operations and Reporting Coordinator | Wexmoor Property Management, Columbus, OH | Apr 2021 to Present
• Schedules maintenance, landscaping and cleaning vendors for 18 properties and processes about 250 vendor invoices a month, coding each to property and expense category.
• Rebuilt the company's Microsoft Access database in 2024 to hold invoices, work orders and vendor contracts in linked tables, and writes SQL queries in Access (inner and outer joins, aggregates, parameter queries) for questions from the owners and property managers.
• Set up a Power Query connection from Excel to the Access tables so the monthly spending summary by property and category refreshes in minutes instead of half a day of retyping.
• Built a Power BI report in early 2026 on top of the same tables, with pages for spending against budget by property, open work orders by days open and vendor cost per unit; the two owners use it in place of the printed packet at the monthly review.
• Compared occupancy and turnover days by building from AppFolio exports joined to work order history, and showed that units waiting on paint and flooring vendors sat vacant about nine days longer; the owners added a second flooring vendor.
• Pulled three years of landscaping and snow removal invoices by property and showed that two vendors were billing per visit at rates well above the flat contracts at other buildings. The owners rebid both contracts, saving about $38,000 a year.
• Prepares the weekly open work order report by property and days open, now with a chart of median days to close, which the operations manager reviews every Monday.
• Charted work order counts by category and construction year for the 2025 annual review; rising plumbing calls at two older buildings supported a $120,000 pipe replacement budget.
• Found about 70 work orders coded to the wrong property after a software update and worked with the AppFolio administrator to correct the property list.
• Maintains vendor insurance certificate and contract end date records, with a query that lists anything expiring in the next 60 days.

Leasing Assistant | Wexmoor Property Management, Columbus, OH | Aug 2019 to Mar 2021
• Answered leasing calls and emails, scheduled tours and entered rental applications into AppFolio.
• Updated the weekly vacancy list in Excel for the leasing manager, adding days vacant and advertised rent.
• Sent renewal reminder letters 90 and 60 days before lease end and tracked responses in a spreadsheet.
• Filed lease documents and kept move-in and move-out checklists current.

Office Assistant (part time) | Quarry Lane Insurance Agency, Columbus, OH | Sep 2017 to May 2019
• Answered phones, scanned policy documents and updated client contact records.
• Kept a spreadsheet log of incoming mail and payments for the office manager.
• Helped convert paper client files to the agency's document system, indexing about 1,500 files over one summer.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2019

SKILLS
Data: SQL in Microsoft Access (inner and outer joins, GROUP BY, subqueries, parameter queries), table design and relationships, Power Query
BI: Power BI Desktop (one report in regular use, basic DAX measures)
Spreadsheets: Excel (pivot tables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, charts), Google Sheets
Property systems: AppFolio, vendor scheduling calendars, invoice coding
Other: vendor communication, budget tracking, record keeping

ADDITIONAL
• Earned an Excel Expert badge through an online course, 2024
• Completed an online Power BI fundamentals course, 2026
• Volunteer with a Columbus neighborhood cleanup group, keeping the sign-up sheet and supply counts for monthly events
